title: The 10 Best Corded Detail Sanders
subtitle: Mouse and detail sanders with pointed pads for corners, trim, spindles and furniture, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A detail sander (often called a mouse sander) has an iron-shaped pad that reaches into corners, along trim and between spindles where a round orbital pad can't. We ranked 10 corded best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (extra detail attachments, a vacuum port and hook-and-loop paper). Most run 12,000 to 16,000 orbits per minute, so the real differences are attachments, dust collection and the sheets in the box. They run from about $21 for WEN's 6301 to $59 for CRAFTSMAN's CMEW210.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: DEKOPRO 1.5A Mouse Sander, Corded Palm Sander with Dust Collection & 15pc Sandpapers
avoid.flag: Lowest rating; dust claims walked back on the listing
avoid.verdict: A budget mouse sander that sells well but rates worst. For 50 cents less, the GALAX has 4.5 stars and 20 sheets.
reasons: It's rated 3.9 stars, the lowest of the 12 detail sanders we compared, while sanders within a few dollars of it are rated 4.3 to 4.5.
The listing advertises an '11-hole efficient dust collection system', then says in the same bullet that it 'cannot collect all the dust' and tells you to hook up a vacuum.
It lists no voltage, weight or warranty, and the spec table names sandpaper as the only included component even though the bullets add a dust collector.

buyers_guide.q: Detail sander or random orbital sander?
buyers_guide.a: A random orbital sander is faster and leaves a better finish on flat panels. A detail sander's pointed pad gets into corners, along trim and between spindles. Many people own both.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need the extra attachments?
buyers_guide.a: Only for furniture and trim. A finger attachment gets between chair slats and spindles; a contour pad follows curves. For corners and edges, the standard pad is enough.
A little. Faster pads remove material quicker, but every sander here runs 12,000 to 16,000 opm. Dust collection and paper quality make more difference.
Detail sanders use pre-cut hook-and-loop sheets shaped like the pad. Buy sheets that match the pad size and hole pattern so dust collection works.

buyers_guide.q: Will a detail sander strip paint?
buyers_guide.a: It will for small areas like window frames and trim, with 60 or 80 grit. For large painted surfaces a random orbital or belt sander is much faster. Test old paint for lead before sanding it.
